title: The Burnt Mill
description: Everybody in Rivermark can tell you the mill burned. Nobody can tell you which year, and nobody has been out to look since it happened.

go_and_look.title: Go and look
go_and_look.objective: Walk out to the mill on the ford road and see what is actually there.
go_and_look.journal: The mill is a fact in every conversation in Rivermark and nobody has walked the two miles. Three walls, a wheel-pit full of black water, and a race that still runs perfectly well past a building that has not needed it in four years.

the_counting_loft.title: Where it started
the_counting_loft.objective: Work out where the fire began.
the_counting_loft.journal: Every charred beam-end in the wall points inward. A kiln fire spreads out from the kiln and takes the floor above it; this one started high on the river side, in the counting loft, where the mill kept its paper and no fire was ever lit.

found_the_cause.title: It started in the loft
found_the_cause.journal: It started in the counting loft, on the river side, where the mill kept its books and nobody ever struck a light. The stones are scorched in a corner that had no lamp, no flue and no reason. I have written it down. It does not tell me who, and I have stopped expecting it to.

made_it_a_shelter.title: A roof on the road
made_it_a_shelter.journal: We cleared the roof-fall out of the south end, put hurdles across the gap and a slate over the fire-back, and told the drovers at the fold that there was a dry wall two miles up the road. Four of them used it inside a week. It is not an answer to anything. It is a room.

left_the_mill.title: Left standing
left_the_mill.journal: Three walls and running water. I went out, I looked, I came back, and I am now one more person in Rivermark who can say that the mill burned.
